Answer: B
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates marked hyperlucency of the right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings and a smaller right hilum, which are classic features of Swyer–James–MacLeod syndrome (post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans). This condition is strongly associated with a history of recurrent lung infections in childhood and can lead to bronchiectasis.
